public_rationale: On July 29, 2026, Microsoft reported that its April–June 2026 results, adjusted for specified discrete items, exceeded management guidance for revenue, operating income and diluted earnings per share [e1]. Those earlier quarterly results cannot establish whether the labs will fall short of the revenue threshold by the contract's August 11, 2030 deadline or whether the named hyperscalers will miss the relevant analyst and investor expectations [e1; resolution contract]. The disclosure also does not establish the claimed financing necessity or an event meeting the contract's early-resolution rule [e1; resolution contract].
limitations: The evidence does not establish the conditional antecedent across the full four-year horizon.
The revenue comparison lacks a fixed aggregation, comparator year, reporting scope and accounting basis.
No corresponding expectations series fixed at publication was established.
An earlier result against management guidance does not test the specified future analyst and investor expectations.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic's expected compute spend requires them to earn as much revenue as Microsoft, Google and Amazon within four years; if they don't, hyperscalers will miss analyst and investor expectations.
conditions: if OpenAI and Anthropic don't reach hyperscaler-level revenue

statement.excerpt: No matter how big, handsome, and amazing you think either of these companies are, their expected compute spend will require them to make as much revenue as Microsoft, Google and Amazon in the next four years, and if they don’t, hyperscalers will not meet analyst and investor expectations.

from_speaker: as much revenue as Microsoft, Google and Amazon
hyperscalers will not meet analyst and investor expectations
our_interpretation: The four-year horizon ends on August 11, 2030.
Revenue ordinarily means realized annual company revenue, not an annualized monthly run rate, financing, or valuation.

A provisional collective reading compares the labs' combined annual revenue with the named companies' combined annual revenue. The wording does not settle this against an individual-company comparison.
The comparator year and whether Google means Alphabet or a narrower business are unspecified.
Expectations should be those identifiable at publication for the relevant future results, rather than estimates revised after the outcomes.
The hyperscaler forecast's antecedent is failure to reach the revenue threshold within four years; a shortfall in 2026 cannot establish that antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: After fixing the comparison and expectations measures, the labs fail to reach the stated revenue threshold by the deadline and the named hyperscalers miss the corresponding expectations. Establishing that the revenue level was necessary also requires a financing and compute-cost analysis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The labs remain below the agreed revenue threshold through the deadline while the named hyperscalers meet the relevant expectations, or the labs demonstrably finance and fulfill the expected compute spending without the claimed revenue scale.
